summary: Preview-only regression + new-feature testing for the ORA browser diagnostic tool round. All 20 real (non-mocked) browser E2E tests pass (real navigations to https://example.com and https://httpbin.org/forms/post, real 500 capture, SSRF/scheme blocking for 127.0.0.1/10./172.16./192.168./169.254./localhost/[::1] and file://data:/ftp://, fresh-profile isolation, browser close on turn end, invalid/too-many-steps rejected, honest degradation when browser unavailable). Wiring audit (12), AskAdvisor unchanged (7), ship-meter (4), and the full -k filter regression (loop_safety | ship_meter | output_guard | pending_action | insert_edit | ask_advisor | browser_diagnostic | wiring_audit) all green: 85 passed / 12 skipped / 0 failed / 7246 deselected. Frontend vitest for Settings TrackSwitcher gate + /build routes alive: 5/5 passed. Frontend Settings visual smoke was NOT captured because preview login with test@aurem.dev / AuremTest2026! did not authenticate (redirected back to /login?next=/settings) — this appears to be a stale-credential issue not caused by this round's changes; the vitest DOM assertions already prove TRACK_SWITCHER_ENABLED=false gates the TrackSwitcher render, component definition is preserved, and /build + personal/* routes remain registered. Concurrency-lock (project_busy) path in services/browser_tools.py has no dedicated automated test — flagged as LOW-priority gap per request. Chromium binary production availability remains UNVERIFIED for the deployed image (disclosed risk, no Docker changes allowed).

minor.issue: No dedicated automated test for the acquire-loop-lock wait → 'project_busy' error branch. All other paths (SSRF, scheme block, fresh profile, browser-close, degradation) are covered.

critical_code_review_comments: services/browser_tools.py SSRF gate correctly blocks all RFC1918, loopback (v4+v6), link-local (169.254/16) and non-http(s) schemes — verified by 11 SSRF/scheme tests. Good defense in depth.
Fresh browser profile + finally: await browser.close() per _run_steps invocation is a clean isolation model; test_t_browser_closes_after_turn confirms no cookie/localStorage bleed.

Concurrency safety correctly reuses services/loop_safety.acquire_loop_lock so a browser check and a Loop ship on the same project_id cannot race — but the 'project_busy' error branch itself has no direct test; add one to lock the behavior.

Tool wiring is coherent across the three registration points (LOCAL_TOOLS dispatch, TOOL_SPECS list, tools_bridge._KNOWN_TOOLS) — wiring_audit tests enforce spec↔handler bijection which will catch future drift.
AskAdvisor comment-only edit truly is behavior-preserving (6 tests including SSE thinking/done frames, GLM provider meta frame, and ORA-branch-does-not-fall-through-to-orchestrator all still pass).
